summary: Update the URL-normalization guide to match the current implementation, including percent-encoded UTM parameter names.
rationale: The existing feature document incorrectly says URLs are saved unchanged. The current creation flow normalizes new destinations before saving them, and removes UTM parameters when their names begin with utm_ after percent-decoding. Updating the existing document keeps the user and operator guidance accurate without creating conflicting documentation.
content:
## URL normalization when creating links

### What it does

When a new link is created, the service normalizes its destination before saving it:

- Lowercases the URL scheme and host.
- Removes port 80 from HTTP URLs and port 443 from HTTPS URLs. Other ports are retained.
- Removes query parameters whose names begin with `utm_`, case-insensitively. The parameter name is percent-decoded before this check, so encoded forms such as `%75tm_source` and `UTM%5Fcampaign` are also removed.

Other query parameters are preserved in their original order and representation. Path casing and fragments are preserved. If all query parameters are removed, the URL has no query string. A parameter is filtered by its name, not its value; for example, `x_utm_source=keep` and `value=utm_source` are retained.

### API usage

Create a link with `POST /api/v1/links` using the existing request shape:

```http
POST /api/v1/links
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "longUrl": "HTTPS://Example.COM:443/docs?utm_source=mail&ref=home#Section"
}
```

The endpoint returns `201 Created`. The `longUrl` in the response is the normalized, saved destination; generated link values vary:

```json
{
  "code": "Abc1234",
  "shortUrl": "https://shortener.example/Abc1234",
  "longUrl": "https://example.com/docs?ref=home#Section",
  "createdAt": "2026-10-20T12:00:00Z",
  "expiresAt": null
}
```

Encoded UTM names are also removed. For example, this destination:

```text
HTTPS://Example.COM:443/docs?keep=%2f&%75tm_source=mail&UTM%5Fcampaign=spring&x_utm_source=retain#Section
```

is saved and returned as:

```text
https://example.com/docs?keep=%2f&x_utm_source=retain#Section
```

`GET /api/v1/links/{code}` returns the saved normalized destination in its `longUrl` field. `GET /{code}` redirects to that saved destination. The request and response shapes and endpoint statuses are otherwise unchanged.

### Configuration

There is no URL-normalization configuration option. Normalization is applied automatically to new links during creation. Existing URL validation and rejection of links targeting the service itself still apply.

### Limitations

- Normalization applies to newly created links only. Existing stored destinations are not rewritten, and no migration is performed.
- Only query segments separated by `&` are considered parameters. A segment is removed when its percent-decoded name starts with `utm_`, ignoring case; values are not inspected.
- Retained query segments are preserved as supplied, including their order and encoding. Path casing and fragments are also preserved.
- Idempotency request hashing uses the original request. Different request bodies that normalize to the same destination can therefore still be treated as different payloads for an idempotency key.
- The destination must still pass the existing absolute HTTP(S) URL validation and cannot point to the service itself.
